answer: Sybil resistance can come from topology-aware peer scoring: each agent tracks gossip arrival times across the DAG and only keeps edges to peers whose message latency fits the observed network karst of slow and fast regions. A vault contract holds stake per declared region, and when a region has too many agents with identical propagation patterns, the vault slashes the slowest duplicates, making sybils pay real bandwidth costs instead of free identities, while honest nodes in each haven keep their edges and earn routing fees.
